name: Self-employed (Scotland)

items.label: Class 4 National Insurance
items.note: Self-employed National Insurance on profits: 6% between £12,570 and £50,270 and 2% above. Paid through Self Assessment, not PAYE. Class 2 is treated as paid on profits of £7,105 or more, so there's nothing to pay.

assumptions: Self-employed sole trader: the figure is taxable profit, after allowable expenses
No other income, and nothing already paid through PAYE
Profits of £7,105 or more, so Class 2 National Insurance is treated as paid
No student loan or pension contribution unless one is chosen
notModelled: Voluntary Class 2 contributions (£3.65 a week) on profits under £7,105
Higher-rate relief on personal pension contributions, which is claimed through Self Assessment
Trading allowance, losses, capital allowances and other adjustments to profit
When the tax is paid: payments on account are worked out separately on the self-employed pages

obtainedFrom.title: Self-employed National Insurance rates (GOV.UK)
obtainedFrom.note: Read 16 Nov 2026, tax year 2026 to 2027: Class 4 6% on profits over £12,570 up to £50,270 and 2% over £50,270; Class 2 treated as paid on profits of £7,105 or more, voluntary £3.65 a week below that.
